claims.text: A perturbation-based free-energy scheme using a machine-learning potential can replace full thermodynamic integration for Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloys.
Training the MLP on liquid-phase local structural descriptors will provide accurate free-energy differences.
Constraining the MLP with enthalpy of mixing and atomic-size difference will prevent overfitting to solid-state configurations.
Ta-Nb-Mo-W-V can be treated as a Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy in a disordered solid-solution state approaching melting.
The thermodynamic descriptors ΔHmix and δ can be obtained from Miedema-model and CALPHAD assessments.
An approximate solidus-to-liquidus range of 2400–3000 K is appropriate for the stated Ta-based systems.
Standard EAM potentials or potentials trained only on crystalline data fail to capture the complex liquid structure of multicomponent refractory alloys.
Liquid local coordination and bond-orientational order are critical structural features distinguishing liquid entropy from solid entropy.
An MLP can learn the complex many-body interactions in the liquid phase that standard EAM misses.
Learning these interactions permits efficient sampling of liquid phase space through perturbation rather than full thermodynamic integration.
ΔHmix and δ constraints make the potential respect thermodynamic stability limits.
ΔHmix and δ constraints prevent artificial stabilization of solid phases in the liquid regime.
The N(N-1)/2 binary interactions in a multicomponent alloy drive intermetallic-phase formation.
The constrained-MLP perturbation scheme will predict melting temperature and free-energy differences within 2% of an accurate ab initio result.
The constrained-MLP perturbation scheme will reduce computational cost by more than 90% relative to full thermodynamic integration.
The approach applies to equimolar or near-equimolar four- to six-component systems because their configurational entropy is high.
The approach fails when the training set lacks sufficient liquid-phase structural diversity.
The approach fails when extreme liquid phase separation is not represented by the training descriptors.

A failure mode of TOR-TILD or similar approaches in multicomponent spaces is extrapolation to liquid configurations absent from the potential's training set, producing artifacts in free-energy differences.
Full ab initio thermodynamic integration is prohibitively expensive for the proposed alloy and limits computational throughput.

contradictions.description: The proposed successful intervention explicitly requires liquid-enriched training, but the falsification experiment trains the MLP only on solid BCC configurations and treats failure of that out-of-scope model as falsification of the liquid-trained hypothesis.
The prediction requires accuracy within 2%, whereas falsification occurs only above 5%; errors between 2% and 5% violate the prediction without triggering the stated falsification rule.
